headline: Adjusted earnings hold steady, GAAP profit dips on hedging
summary_short: Expand Energy posted Q2 2026 revenue of $2,960M (-19.7% y/y) and GAAP net income of $522M ($2.19 diluted EPS), down sharply y/y as unrealized derivative gains fell to $449M from $877M; adjusted EBITDAX held roughly flat at $1,183M (+0.6% y/y).
summary_long: GAAP net income fell to $522M ($2.19 diluted EPS) from $968M a year ago and $1,159M q/q — mainly because derivative gains shrank to $449M from $877M, not from operating deterioration: adjusted EBITDAX held roughly flat at $1,183M (+0.6% y/y) and adjusted net income rose to $317M from $265M. Revenue fell to $2,960M as realized gas price dropped to $2.90/Mcf even as production rose to 7.48 Bcfe/d; FY2026 production guidance was reaffirmed at 7.4-7.6 Bcfe/d. Total debt fell to $3.7B from $5.0B at year-end (April note redemption), leaving net debt at $3.1B (0.5x leverage). Expand also announced the Twin Eagle acquisition and a new $1B buyback authorization.

drivers.explanation: CEO Wichterich cites a peer-leading leverage ratio, a 4% reduction in shares outstanding via buybacks, and the pending Twin Eagle acquisition as this quarter's key strategic moves toward becoming the leading integrated natural gas company.

The decline is price-driven: realized natural gas price fell to $2.90/Mcf (NYMEX averaged $2.90 vs $3.44 y/y) even as net production rose 3.9% y/y to 7.48 Bcfe/d, per the production and pricing tables.

The y/y and q/q declines are explained almost entirely by smaller derivative gains ($449M vs $877M y/y on the income statement), not by operating performance — adjusted net income, which excludes unrealized derivative swings, rose to $317M from $265M.
Moves in line with net income; diluted share count was little changed (238.4M vs 240.6M y/y) despite the quarter's buybacks.

Not explained in the release as a distinct line — this is a Yahoo-sourced shard figure; the release's own GAAP 'Income from operations' reads $661M for the quarter. See confidence_notes for the reconciliation gap.

No explicit narrative driver given; this company-disclosed non-GAAP metric holding flat y/y while net income fell confirms the net income drop is a derivative/GAAP-accounting effect rather than an operating one.
